content: Rilpivirine is a medication used in combination with other drugs to manage HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, which helps improve the function of the immune system. This, in turn, lowers the risk of developing complications related to HIV, such as new infections or certain cancers, and enhances overall quality of life. Rilpivirine is typically prescribed to individuals who have not previously taken HIV medications. It belongs to a class of drugs known as non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). However, it is important to note that rilpivirine is not a cure for HIV infection. To minimize the risk of transmitting HIV to others, it is essential to continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Additionally, use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your healthcare provider. Avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may come into contact with blood or other bodily fluids. Before starting rilpivirine, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication by mouth with a meal, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The dosage may depend on other medications you are taking. Certain drugs that reduce or block stomach acid, such as proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), H2 blockers, or antacids, can decrease the absorption of rilpivirine, making it less effective. Avoid taking PPIs (e.g., omeprazole, lansoprazole) while on rilpivirine. It is crucial to take rilpivirine and other HIV medications exactly as prescribed. Do not reduce the dose, stop taking the medication, or increase the dose without consulting your doctor, even for a short period. For optimal results, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals. If you miss a dose, take it with a meal as soon as you remember. However, if more than 12 hours have passed since the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store rilpivirine in its original bottle at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into drains unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused medication. While taking rilpivirine, regular medical and laboratory tests, such as viral load, T-cell counts, and liver function tests, are necessary to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. Common side effects of rilpivirine include headaches and difficulty sleeping. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off previously existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Changes in body fat distribution, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach or decreased fat in the arms and legs, may also occur, though the cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Rilpivirine can sometimes cause a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it is important to distinguish this from a rare rash that may indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to rilpivirine are rare but possible. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking rilpivirine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you are pregnant, discuss the use of this medication with your doctor, as treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Rilpivirine passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor about breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how rilpivirine works or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications, such as dexamethasone, macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), and rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifapentine), can affect the removal of rilpivirine from your body, potentially impacting its effectiveness. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about rilpivirine. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
